title: Partial labels and abstain guidelines (notebook)
notes:
Context:
This is a working notebook for handling partial/fragmented labels and explicit abstain reasons in our annotation UI. Goal is to define pragmatic heuristics that reduce reviewer churn and make gold/consensus sets repeatable across messy inputs (HTML fragments, truncated copy, OCR noise).

High-level problem statement:
- We see a lot of examples where a single logical entity is only partially present (e.g., person name missing surname, url truncated, duplicate tokens split by punctuation).
- Labelers either: (a) mark the partial span, (b) expand to nearest meaningful context, or (c) abstain. This variability pollutes model training.

Guiding principles (draft):
1) Prefer conservative positive labeling for partial-but-clear signals: if >50% of a canonical token is present and intent is unambiguous, allow partial positive.
2) Use explicit "ABSTAIN" with reason codes when labeler is "not sure" or when the item is likely corrupt (OCR artifacts, redaction placeholders).
3) Capture normalization hints: when selecting partial spans, labelers should add a short normalization token in comment (e.g., "john.doe -> John Doe (partial)").
4) Consensus rules: two labelers agreeing on span overlap >= 0.6 and same label type => accept; else escalate to reviewer.

Suggested abstain reason codes (short list to add to UI):
- ABSTAIN_NO_CONTEXT  -- not enough surrounding text
- ABSTAIN_TRUNCATED   -- truncated token / url / email
- ABSTAIN_OCR_NOISE   -- heavy OCR / garbage characters
- ABSTAIN_REDIRECT    -- placeholder like [redacted] or XXXX
- ABSTAIN_AMBIGUOUS   -- multiple plausible labels, cannot choose

Heuristics for resolving partial spans (implementation notes):
- If two spans overlap and one is substring of the other, prefer the longer span unless shorter is annotated with "partial-flag" comment.
- Canonicalization pipeline: store raw span + normalized form. Normalizer rules: case-unfold, remove trailing punctuation, map common OCR confusions (0/O, 1/I). Keep both raw and normalized in dataset.
- For URLs/emails: if scheme or domain fragment present and > 60% of domain chars present, allow label but mark as "partial_url". That helps downstream model learn to complete.

UI / workflow suggestions (quick):
- Add a small dropdown next to each label for "Quality/Reason" with the reason codes above. Required when selecting "ABSTAIN".
- Inline quick-normalize button: pop a text field prefilled with suggested normalization (auto from rule); labeler can edit. Save both values.
- Show overlap indicator when other annotator previously marked overlapping spans (to encourage consistency).

Sampling strategy to capture long-tail partials (experiments):
1) Query sample: search corpus for tokens with punctuation at ends (endswith: ".,;:") and capture 2k examples.
2) OCR-prone sample: use source metadata to pull documents from OCR ingestion queues (estimated 5% of corpus).
3) Truncated content: heuristics: lines shorter than 30 chars and last char not whitespace; validate 1k examples.
Goal: create 5k-target set with enriched annotations for edge heuristics.

Evaluation / metrics to validate rules:
- Inter-annotator agreement (IAA) before vs after rules: span IoU and label type F1. Target: increase IoU by +0.08 on partial-class examples.
- Abstain rate: expect initial bump as labelers adopt codes; aim to reduce by 25% after clarifications and examples.
- Post-normalization model utility: train quick probe to predict full canonical form from partials; measure top-1/full-recovery rate.

Example annotation cases (quick):
1) "Jon D." in body referring to "Jon Daniel" elsewhere -> label as PERSON span "Jon D." with normalization "Jon Daniel (inferred)" and reason code "partial-flag".
2) "https://exampl" (line cut) -> label as URL span with "partial_url" flag and ABSTAIN_TRUNCATED if unsure.
3) "J0hn Smith" from OCR -> label as PERSON, note normalization "John Smith" and reason ABSTAIN_OCR_NOISE if uncertain.
4) "[redacted name]" -> ABSTAIN_REDIRECT, do not create pseudo-spans.

Reviewer workflow (proposal):
- Auto-accept rules: if 2+ labelers match type and normalized value matches (exact) -> auto-promote to gold.
- Escalation: if disagreement in type or normalization -> send to reviewer queue with both annotations and labeler comments. Aim SLAs: 48h for triage.

Open questions / to discuss:
- Thresholds: 50% vs 60% overlap for allowing partial positives? Need quick sim on held-out sample to pick sweet spot.
- How strict should normalization be? Free-text vs constrained suggestions?
- Enforcement: make ABSTAIN reason required for any abstain; how to prevent gaming?

Immediate TODOs (short):

- [ ] Add 5 canonical examples per code to UI help text (owner: Lina) -- target: 2024-10-05

Notes-to-self:

End of notebook.
